name: sysdig-remediate
conclusion: sysdig-remediate (Escalate) specifies 5 of 5 categories: 8 autonomy limits, 8 clarification rules, 10+ approval gates, 2 validation rules, 9 escalation rules. Strongest: approval gates.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 8 autonomy limits (8 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly prose: allowed tools; proceeding after the preamble; commits or PRs to unowned repos.

statements.quote: allowed-tools:
After presenting the preamble, proceed directly to step 0b — the preamble is informational, do not ask for confirmation.
NEVER commit or open PRs/MRs to repos that are not owned by the user or by an org/group the user belongs to.
No branch, no commit, no push — the user reviews and applies the diff themselves.
Do not run `git commit`, `git push`, or modify any branch.
**Never remove or modify the existing description.** Always append new information below the existing content.
**Never create tickets in this skill.** Ticket creation lives in `/sysdig-investigate`. This skill only updates the ticket referenced by the optional `ticket` input argument.
When updating an existing ticket, NEVER remove or modify the original description — always append below a separator (`----`).

clarification_rules.conclusion: 8 clarification rules (7 mandatory, 1 advisory; 6 conditional), mostly list: missing image; resume suggestion from remediation history; multiple ticket matches.

statements.quote: Interactively: if no image is provided, ask the user to specify one or run `/sysdig-investigate` to select from the investigation list.

If `remediation_history` has at least one entry from the last 14 days, surface a resume summary to the user before continuing — name the most recent image, the date, the PR or ticket key if present, a
**Multiple matches** — present the top 3 and let the user pick one or skip.
If found and less than 30 days old, propose it to the user for confirmation.
If no confident match is found, ask one question at a time:
First, present the top candidate repos: _"I found these repositories that might own this image: `<list>`. Which one, or none of these?"_
Only if the user picks "none of these", ask the follow-up: _"Switch to local-folder mode? Provide a path, or cancel."_
Never guess a repo mapping — if not confident, ask the user.

approval_gates.conclusion: 10+ approval gates (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly list: skill handoffs; writes such as branches, commits and PRs; searching for an open ticket.

statements.quote: **Announce every skill handoff.** Before invoking another skill, name it explicitly and summarize what it'll do, then wait for confirmation.
**Pause for confirmation before any write.** Branch creation, commits, PR/MR opens, and ticket updates all require an explicit user yes. Read-only queries do not.
Otherwise, ask the user (default **No**): _"No ticket was passed. Search for an open ticket related to `<image_name>` first?"_
**Exactly one match** — show its key, summary, and assignee; ask the user to confirm adopting it.
IMPORTANT: If the repo does not belong to the user or any of their organizations/groups, WARN the user and ask whether to continue.
Store `suggested_reviewers` and present them to the user for confirmation before setting them — the user can accept, change, or skip.
Present the user with the proposed action before doing anything:
If a PR is possible (Case A or B) and the user confirms, go to step 4a.

**Show the diff before opening.** Print the full file diff (`git diff <default-branch>..HEAD`) and the rendered PR body inline, then pause for an explicit user yes. A summary is not a substitute for t
**Reviewers:** if `suggested_reviewers` was populated in step 3b, request review from those users (after confirming with the user).

validation.conclusion: 2 validation rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 0 conditional), mostly list: fix versions introducing new vulnerabilities; fix chain analysis before upgrades.

statements.quote: Before proposing any fix, verify that the candidate fix version does not itself introduce new Critical or High vulnerabilities.
Always run the fix chain analysis (step 3c) before proposing any version upgrade — never suggest a fix version without first verifying it is clean.

escalation.conclusion: 9 escalation rules (9 mandatory, 0 advisory; 8 conditional), mostly prose: Sysdig MCP authentication preflight; failed Sysdig MCP check; failed source control check.

statements.quote: **Sysdig MCP authentication preflight** — required. Run the preflight in [`references/auth-preflight.md`](references/auth-preflight.md) and follow its instructions exactly. If it tells you to abort, a
If the **Sysdig MCP** check fails, do not proceed — the diagnostic checklist above will have already reported the specific problem and fix.
If the **source control** check fails (no forge configured and the user cannot provide a local folder), stop with:
Skip the search strategies below, verify the working tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty — refuse if dirty), and go to step 3a.
| C | No safe fix version available | No PR — append analysis to ticket (if set), otherwise stop and refer to `/sysdig-investigate` |
| D | Repo not located within configured source | No PR — offer local mode, otherwise escalate via ticket / `/sysdig-investigate` |
If the ticket update fails, report it in the canonical what / why / fix shape, then continue — do not block on the ticket update:
In Case C/D (no PR possible) with no ticket key set (neither passed via `ticket:` nor adopted in step 1b), stop and tell the user to run `/sysdig-investigate` to file a tracking ticket.
